# Purpose

This notebook audits the supplementary Home Credit tables before they are used
for feature engineering. Each table is analyzed at its native grain and is not
joined to the application tables until its keys and timing fields are checked.
The outcome, `TARGET`, is used only for later modeling—not to construct any
supplementary-table feature in this EDA.

# Setup and data inventory

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: true
#| output: true
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)

files <- c(
  application_train = "application_train.csv",
  application_test = "application_test.csv",
  bureau = "bureau.csv",
  bureau_balance = "bureau_balance.csv",
  credit_card_balance = "credit_card_balance.csv",
  installments_payments = "installments_payments.csv",
  POS_CASH_balance = "POS_CASH_balance.csv",
  previous_application = "previous_application.csv",
  sample_submission = "sample_submission.csv"
)

missing_files <- files[!file.exists(files)]
if (length(missing_files)) {
  stop("Missing required files: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

file_inventory <- tibble(
  table = names(files),
  file = unname(files),
  size_mb = round(file.info(files)$size / 1024^2, 1)
)
print(file_inventory)

# Read one supplemental table at a time. Several tables are large, so remove
# objects after each section instead of retaining every raw table in memory.
read_table <- function(file) read_csv(file, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)

# Return a compact structural and missingness audit for any table.
audit_table <- function(data, table_name, key_columns) {
  overview <- tibble(
    table = table_name,
    rows = nrow(data),
    columns = ncol(data),
    key_columns = paste(intersect(key_columns, names(data)), collapse = ", ")
  )
  missingness <- tibble(
    column = names(data),
    missing_pct = map_dbl(data, ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100),
    distinct_values = map_int(data, ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) |>
    arrange(desc(missing_pct))
  list(overview = overview, missingness = missingness)
}

train_keys <- read_table(files[["application_train"]]) |> select(SK_ID_CURR, TARGET)
test_keys <- read_table(files[["application_test"]]) |> select(SK_ID_CURR)
```

# Relationship map

| Table | Native grain | Application key | Secondary key | Main timing field |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bureau` | One bureau credit record | `SK_ID_CURR` | `SK_ID_BUREAU` | `DAYS_CREDIT` |
| `bureau_balance` | One bureau-credit month | Indirect via bureau | `SK_ID_BUREAU` | `MONTHS_BALANCE` |
| `previous_application` | One prior application | `SK_ID_CURR` | `SK_ID_PREV` | `DAYS_DECISION` |
| `POS_CASH_balance` | One prior-loan month | `SK_ID_CURR` | `SK_ID_PREV` | `MONTHS_BALANCE` |
| `credit_card_balance` | One prior-card month | `SK_ID_CURR` | `SK_ID_PREV` | `MONTHS_BALANCE` |
| `installments_payments` | One scheduled installment/payment | `SK_ID_CURR` | `SK_ID_PREV` | `DAYS_INSTALMENT`, `DAYS_ENTRY_PAYMENT` |
| `sample_submission` | One test application | `SK_ID_CURR` | — | — |

All timing fields are relative to the current application. A value of zero or a
positive value must be reviewed before use because it may be concurrent with or
after the current application and could cause leakage.

# Question 1: Are keys complete and are child tables linked to valid applications?

```{r}
#| label: key-coverage
#| echo: true
supplemental_specs <- tribble(
  ~table, ~file, ~key, ~parent_key,
  "bureau", files[["bureau"]], "SK_ID_CURR", NA_character_,
  "bureau_balance", files[["bureau_balance"]], "SK_ID_BUREAU", "bureau.csv",
  "credit_card_balance", files[["credit_card_balance"]], "SK_ID_CURR", NA_character_,
  "installments_payments", files[["installments_payments"]], "SK_ID_CURR", NA_character_,
  "POS_CASH_balance", files[["POS_CASH_balance"]], "SK_ID_CURR", NA_character_,
  "previous_application", files[["previous_application"]], "SK_ID_CURR", NA_character_
)

key_audit <- pmap_dfr(supplemental_specs, function(table, file, key, parent_key) {
  data <- read_table(file)
  result <- tibble(
    table = table,
    rows = nrow(data),
    null_key = sum(is.na(data[[key]])),
    distinct_key = n_distinct(data[[key]], na.rm = TRUE),
    duplicate_key_rows = sum(duplicated(data[[key]]))
  )
  rm(data); gc(FALSE)
  result
})
print(key_audit)
```

Duplicate values are expected for monthly and payment-level tables. The audit
identifies their grain; it does not imply that duplicates are data errors.

# Question 2: What are the coverage, missingness, and timing characteristics of each table?

## Bureau credit records

```{r}
#| label: bureau-eda
bureau <- read_table(files[["bureau"]])
bureau_audit <- audit_table(bureau, "bureau", c("SK_ID_CURR", "SK_ID_BUREAU"))
print(bureau_audit$overview)
print(slice_head(bureau_audit$missingness, n = 12))

bureau_summary <- bureau |>
  mutate(
    current_application_coverage = SK_ID_CURR %in% train_keys$SK_ID_CURR,
    debt_to_credit = if_else(AMT_CREDIT_SUM > 0, AMT_CREDIT_SUM_DEBT / AMT_CREDIT_SUM, NA_real_),
    nonprior_record = DAYS_CREDIT >= 0
  ) |>
  summarise(
    applications = n_distinct(SK_ID_CURR),
    bureau_records = n(),
    records_per_application = bureau_records / applications,
    nonprior_record_pct = mean(nonprior_record, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    debt_to_credit_missing_pct = mean(is.na(debt_to_credit)) * 100
  )
print(bureau_summary)
# Summarize the most common combinations before plotting the active/closed mix.
print(bureau |> count(CREDIT_ACTIVE, CREDIT_TYPE, sort = TRUE) |> slice_head(n = 20))
bureau |> count(CREDIT_ACTIVE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(CREDIT_ACTIVE, n), y = n, fill = CREDIT_ACTIVE)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Bureau credit records by account status",
    x = "Bureau account status", y = "Number of bureau records"
  )
rm(bureau); gc(FALSE)
```

Interpretation: The summary establishes bureau coverage and whether active,
closed, or sold accounts dominate the available history. A nonzero percentage
of non-prior records requires an explicit leakage rule before bureau features
are aggregated to the current application.

## Bureau monthly status

```{r}
#| label: bureau-balance-eda
bureau_balance <- read_table(files[["bureau_balance"]])
bureau_balance_audit <- audit_table(bureau_balance, "bureau_balance", "SK_ID_BUREAU")
print(bureau_balance_audit$overview)
print(slice_head(bureau_balance_audit$missingness, n = 10))
# Status is categorical; show both the table and a labeled frequency plot.
status_counts <- bureau_balance |> count(STATUS, sort = TRUE)
print(status_counts)
status_counts |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(STATUS, n), y = n, fill = STATUS)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly bureau status distribution",
    x = "Monthly bureau status code", y = "Number of monthly records"
  )
print(bureau_balance |> summarise(
  records = n(),
  bureau_accounts = n_distinct(SK_ID_BUREAU),
  earliest_month = min(MONTHS_BALANCE, na.rm = TRUE),
  latest_month = max(MONTHS_BALANCE, na.rm = TRUE)
))
rm(bureau_balance); gc(FALSE)
```

Interpretation: The status table and plot show whether the monthly history is
mostly closed/unknown/current or contains material delinquency status codes.
The earliest and latest months define the observable history window.

## Previous applications

```{r}
#| label: previous-application-eda
previous <- read_table(files[["previous_application"]])
previous_audit <- audit_table(previous, "previous_application", c("SK_ID_CURR", "SK_ID_PREV"))
print(previous_audit$overview)
print(slice_head(previous_audit$missingness, n = 15))

previous_summary <- previous |>
  mutate(
    application_to_credit = if_else(AMT_CREDIT > 0, AMT_APPLICATION / AMT_CREDIT, NA_real_),
    nonprior_record = DAYS_DECISION >= 0
  ) |>
  summarise(
    applications = n_distinct(SK_ID_CURR), prior_applications = n(),
    applications_per_customer = prior_applications / applications,
    nonprior_record_pct = mean(nonprior_record, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )
print(previous_summary)
# Plot prior-application outcomes to assess the available decision history.
previous_status <- previous |> count(NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS, sort = TRUE)
print(previous |> count(NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS, NAME_CONTRACT_TYPE, sort = TRUE))
previous_status |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS, n), y = n, fill = NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Prior applications by contract status",
    x = "Prior-application status", y = "Number of prior applications"
  )
rm(previous); gc(FALSE)
```

Interpretation: Prior approvals, refusals, and cancellations can be meaningful
history features only when their decision dates precede the current application.
The non-prior percentage flags records that need exclusion or source review.

## Installment payments

```{r}
#| label: installments-eda
installments <- read_table(files[["installments_payments"]])
installment_audit <- audit_table(installments, "installments_payments", c("SK_ID_CURR", "SK_ID_PREV"))
print(installment_audit$overview)
print(slice_head(installment_audit$missingness, n = 10))

installment_summary <- installments |>
  mutate(
    days_late = DAYS_ENTRY_PAYMENT - DAYS_INSTALMENT,
    payment_ratio = if_else(AMT_INSTALMENT > 0, AMT_PAYMENT / AMT_INSTALMENT, NA_real_),
    nonprior_record = DAYS_INSTALMENT >= 0 | DAYS_ENTRY_PAYMENT >= 0
  ) |>
  summarise(
    applications = n_distinct(SK_ID_CURR), payment_rows = n(),
    late_payment_pct = mean(days_late > 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    nonprior_record_pct = mean(nonprior_record, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    median_payment_ratio = median(payment_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
print(installment_summary)
# Use a reproducible sample only for the plot; all summary statistics above use
# the complete table. This prevents a multi-million-row graphic from obscuring
# the distribution.
set.seed(6812)
timing_plot_data <- installments |>
  transmute(days_late = DAYS_ENTRY_PAYMENT - DAYS_INSTALMENT) |>
  filter(is.finite(days_late), days_late >= -100, days_late <= 100)

timing_plot_data |>
  slice_sample(n = min(100000, nrow(timing_plot_data))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = days_late)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "#4C78A8", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of installment payment timing",
    x = "Days late (positive values are late)", y = "Number of payment records"
  )
rm(installments); gc(FALSE)
```

Interpretation: The payment-timing plot reveals whether payments cluster on or
before due dates or have a long late-payment tail. The late-payment percentage
and payment ratio are candidate aggregates, not current-application outcomes.

## POS cash and credit-card monthly balances

```{r}
#| label: monthly-balance-eda
monthly_specs <- tribble(
  ~table, ~file,
  "POS_CASH_balance", files[["POS_CASH_balance"]],
  "credit_card_balance", files[["credit_card_balance"]]
)

pwalk(monthly_specs, function(table, file) {
  data <- read_table(file)
  audit <- audit_table(data, table, c("SK_ID_CURR", "SK_ID_PREV"))
  cat("\n", table, "\n", sep = "")
  print(audit$overview)
  print(slice_head(audit$missingness, n = 10))
  print(data |> summarise(
    applications = n_distinct(SK_ID_CURR), rows = n(),
    earliest_month = min(MONTHS_BALANCE, na.rm = TRUE),
    latest_month = max(MONTHS_BALANCE, na.rm = TRUE),
    any_positive_dpd_pct = mean(SK_DPD > 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ))
  # Plot contract-status frequencies with table-specific titles and axis labels.
  status_counts <- data |> count(NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS, sort = TRUE) |> slice_head(n = 15)
  print(status_counts)
  status_counts |>
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS, n), y = n, fill = NAME_CONTRACT_STATUS)) +
    geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Contract status in", table),
      x = "Contract status", y = "Number of monthly records"
    ) |>
    print()
  rm(data); gc(FALSE)
})
```

Interpretation: These tables show the coverage, recency, delinquency presence,
and contract-status composition of monthly cash and card histories. A positive
delinquency percentage supports creating pre-application delinquency-count or
recency aggregates after timing is confirmed.

# Question 3: Does `sample_submission` match the test-application population?

```{r}
#| label: submission-audit
submission <- read_table(files[["sample_submission"]])
submission_audit <- tibble(
  test_rows = nrow(test_keys),
  submission_rows = nrow(submission),
  duplicate_submission_ids = sum(duplicated(submission$SK_ID_CURR)),
  test_ids_missing_from_submission = sum(!test_keys$SK_ID_CURR %in% submission$SK_ID_CURR),
  submission_ids_not_in_test = sum(!submission$SK_ID_CURR %in% test_keys$SK_ID_CURR)
)
print(submission_audit)

submission_audit |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "check", values_to = "count") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(check, count), y = count, fill = check)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Sample-submission and test-ID reconciliation",
    x = "Reconciliation check", y = "Count"
  )
rm(submission); gc(FALSE)
```

Interpretation: The two mismatch counts should be zero and submission rows
should equal test rows. If they do not, predictions cannot be submitted safely
until the identifier discrepancy is resolved.

# Feature-engineering readiness

The EDA identifies candidate aggregates, but they must be calculated from
records known before the current application. Candidate families include:

- Bureau: count of prior records, active-record count, debt/credit summaries,
  credit-type diversity, and overdue amounts.
- Bureau balance: recent status, delinquency-status counts, and history length,
  joined through `SK_ID_BUREAU`.
- Previous applications: prior-application count, approval/rejection counts,
  prior loan amounts, and decision recency.
- Installments: payment count, lateness, underpayment, and payment-ratio
  summaries.
- POS cash and credit card: delinquency frequency, balance/limit utilization,
  contract-status counts, and recency.

Before implementation, remove or explicitly justify any rows with nonnegative
relative dates, confirm that every child-table key maps to its parent, fit any
imputation or binning on training data only, and aggregate to one row per
`SK_ID_CURR` before joining to application data.
